title: Пуговица в десерте  (A Button in the Dessert)

segments.t: In the dining room, a woman dining with her companion bites into her dessert and pulls out a button, immediately demanding to see the pastry chef and the head chef. Nastya rushes over to tell Max what she discovered, but the dining-room emergency interrupts them.
Блин, что вы меня не разбудили?
Я могу увидеть кондитера и шефа?
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
Блин, что вы меня не разбудили?

'Damn, why did you guys not wake me up?' Wondering if damn why did Louis guys not wake him up shows Barinov caught off guard. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'Come on, come on, hurry.' Because Barinov should come on come on hurry, Louis treats the matter as settled. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
'She ordered a dessert together with it.' Around the moment and dessert, Barinov sets a calm, everyday tone with Louis.
'Enjoy your meal.' Telling Barinov to enjoy Barinov's meal is how Louis lays out the situation for Barinov.
'Oh, excuse me.' Realizing that Louis should excuse him changes how Barinov handles the situation.
'Pardon me, there is some kind of surprise in here.' Since pardon him there is some kind of surprise in here, Louis does not waste words on excuses.
Я могу увидеть кондитера и шефа?

'May I see the pastry chef and the head chef?' Questioning whether may he sees the pastry and the head is how Barinov tests Louis's story. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.

'I wanted to tell you something important.' Louis reminds Barinov that he wanted to tell Barinov something important before the moment passes. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'A guest found a button inside her dessert.' Because a guest found a button inside her dessert, Barinov treats the matter as settled.
'She is asking for the Chef and Louis.' Explaining that she is asking for the Chef and Louis lays the cards on the table for Barinov.

'Let us talk a little later, alright?' Questioning whether they should talk a little later alright is how Barinov tests Louis's story. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
'Alright, follow me.' With the work and dessert in play, Louis keeps this short reply brisk and direct.

'Would you care to explain what this is?' Here checking whether Louis cares to explain what this is shows Barinov looking for the real truth. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
Блин, что вы меня не разбудили?
Я могу увидеть кондитера и шефа?
That wraps up this scene as a guest discovers a button baked into her dessert and demands to see the pastry chef and head chef, interrupting Nastya just as she tries to warn Max. See you next time!
